_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: The Slack hook selector stays visible with a single hook. The VM has one integration, a personal Slack hook "slack-hook". Name elements by ARIA role and accessible name, as Playwright's getByRole does; "named X" means an exact name match. "The modal" is ".integrations-modal". To "open the panel": press Control+k; ".command-palette-input" should be visible; fill it with "integration", click the first ".command-palette-item", and the modal should be visible. To "select" an integration N: click the first ".integrations-tabs button" (the list), then the ".integrations-name-btn" whose text starts with N followed by a space; ".integrations-detail-head strong" should then have exactly the text N. "The refresh button" is the modal's button named "Refresh"; "the Slack test button" is the button named "Test integration (webhook only)"; "the notify button" is the button named "Send test notification". To "close the modal": click the modal's button whose name contains "Close modal". To "start": navigate to /new, wait for the element with data-testid "message-input" to be visible, and open the panel. Perform the steps in order. 1. Start, and select slack-hook. 2. "#slack-hook" should be visible, and the texts of its options should be exactly ["slack-hook · Personal"]. 3. The Slack test button should be visible.
